**The meaning of the verses**
﴿يَا بَنِي آدَمَ خُذُوا زِينَتَكُمْ عِندَ كُلِّ مَسْجِدٍ وَكُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا وَلَا تُسْرِفُوا ۚ إِنَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾

O children of Adam, be in a state of lawful adornment at every prayer, with clothes that cover your private parts, cleanliness, purity and the like; and eat and drink of the good things Allah has provided for you, but do not go beyond the limits of moderation in that. Allah does not love those who go too far and are extravagant in food, drink and other things.

﴿وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًا﴾

And those who, when they spend from their wealth, do not go beyond the limit in giving, nor are tight in spending, and their spending is a middle way between wastefulness and tightness.

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Lina pour water over the courtyard? And how did she answer her mother? And who else in the village said the same as she did?
2. What did Auntie Umm Jamil use to do with her wudu water? And why did she still have water when Karam was thirsty?
3. Is wastefulness only with things there is little of? (No; it is going beyond what is needed, even if the thing is plentiful or belongs to us.) And does that mean being stingy with ourselves? (No; the verse praises the middle way between wastefulness and tightness.)

**This week's exercise**
This week your child is the "water guard" at home: they turn off the tap while scrubbing their hands or brushing their teeth, and turn off any tap they find running for no reason. And try this once: put a bowl under the tap while it runs during the whole of brushing teeth, then once with it turned off, and compare how much collects.
